literal: every year and you are good
usage: This is the standard Egyptian greeting for birthdays, holidays, and special occasions. It is used across all social classes and levels of formality in Cairo. While '3eed meelad sa3eed' is the literal translation of happy birthday, Cairenes overwhelmingly prefer this phrase, adjusting the pronouns for gender and number.

variants.label: to a woman
variants.note: Use this when addressing a woman or girl.

variants.label: to a group
variants.note: Use this when addressing multiple people celebrating together.

variants.label: literal translation
variants.note: A more literal translation used on cakes, greeting cards, or alongside the main phrase.

variants.label: common follow-up
variants.english: May you reach a hundred years
variants.note: A very common follow-up wish said immediately after the main birthday greeting.

responses.english: And you are good (reply to a male)
And you are good (reply to a female)

examples.arabic: كُلَّ سَنَة وَإِنْتَ طَيِّب يَا أَحْمَد، عُقْبَال مِيَّة سَنَة.
examples.transliteration: kull sana w inta tayyib ya a7mad, 3o2bal meyyat sana.
examples.english: Happy birthday Ahmed, may you live to be a hundred.

examples.arabic: النَّهَارْدَة عِيد مِيلَادِك؟ كُلَّ سَنَة وَإِنْتِي طَيِّبَة يَا حَبِيبْتِي!
examples.transliteration: el naharda 3eed meeladek? kull sana w inti tayyiba ya 7abibti!
examples.english: Today is your birthday? Happy birthday my dear!

examples.arabic: كُلَّ سَنَة وَإِنْتُوا طَيِّبِين يَا وِلَاد، هَنَجِيب التُّورْتَة إِمْتَى؟
examples.transliteration: kull sana w intu tayyibeen ya welad, hangeeb el torta emta?
examples.english: Happy birthday boys, when are we getting the cake?
